_top: Policy: only fully human-written posts. Every highlighted block (yellow bar) is AI-written and needs your own words, including the headings. Code blocks, the two latency charts and the timeline diagram are data and can stay. Each section note lists the facts to keep, so you can write from the facts instead of editing my sentences. Scores before the rewrite: Pangram 96% AI, GPTZero 100%, Copyleaks 100%.
_intro: Opening. Pangram's whole AI segment starts here. Write how it really started: who pinged whom, when you first saw coodie in Argus's requirements, how it felt. Facts: coodie had a README, benchmark page, demo apps and an origin post, but no production user; Argus holds the test results QA checks before every release.
argus-and-five-years-of-cqlengine: Facts to keep: Argus is ScyllaDB's test tracking system; SCT longevity runs, dtests and driver matrix jobs report into it (runs, events, packages, results tables, Jira/GitHub issues, release plans). On cqlengine since its first commit, Nov 2021. 47 models, 18 UDTs, all sync, Flask. 35 places used hand-written prepared statements (code sample stays). Alexey Kartashov (maintainer) started the Flask to FastAPI move and hit three limits: no asyncio API, one driver only, no types.
async-this-time-for-real: The most-flagged paragraph of the whole post is in here ("Performance work is never done..."). Facts to keep: coodie.sync and coodie.aio share models, only the Document base class differs. argus#1058 = models to sync coodie, one commit per service; argus#1106 = models to coodie.aio, routes/auth/services become coroutines. Alexey did one perf commit per endpoint. Prometheus data starts Aug 31 (already sync coodie on Flask/uWSGI). FastAPI step: p99 ~1.5 s to under 250 ms, p95 ~450 to ~70 ms, median ~32 ms unchanged. coodie.aio step: submit_run_config 1.1 s to 0.3 s, get_testrun 32 to 19 ms, submit_pytest_result flat (~2M calls in two weeks, single write). p99 under 100 ms most days since. Earlier post measured mapper overhead as small; CI benchmarks on every PR (scylla + acsylla), comment on regressions, history dashboard; next: instruction counting (coodie#323). Your line: perf work is a never-ending story. 35 raw CQL sites mostly gone; leftovers include WRITETIME projection (coodie#330).
pluggable-drivers: The four-driver list is reference data; keep it as a list but put the descriptions in your words. Facts: cqlengine is tied to the DataStax-derived driver. coodie backends: scylla (default, shard-aware), cassandra, acsylla (async, Cython over C++ driver), python-rs (Rust via PyO3, experimental). Switching is one init_coodie argument; async drivers work from the sync API through a bridge. Argus wrapped its existing tuned session (auth, whitelist LB policy, QUORUM profiles) in a CassandraDriver subclass, so cqlengine and coodie shared one session during the migration. You found coodie#329 (execution profiles bug) while writing. The "seam for the future acsylla driver swap" phrase is Alexey's, from the PR: keep it as a quote.
pydantic-types: Facts to keep: cqlengine predates type hints; type checker can't tell what user.roles is. coodie models are Pydantic v2 with Annotated markers; py.typed; validation when the object is built; model_dump() and FastAPI response models. argus#1066 made key and always-populated fields required where data had no NULLs. cqlengine's required=True is runtime-only; in coodie str vs Optional[str] is visible to the type checker before anything runs.
bonus-schema-migrations: Facts to keep: sync_table(dry_run=True) returns the CQL without running it; Argus used it to verify every model, names pinned to cqlengine's (e.g. packageversion_v2); empty result meant no data migration. Drift warnings for unknown DB columns. CLI: schema-diff, makemigration, migrate --dry-run, migrate. Type changes are flagged unsafe: add column, backfill with ctx.scan_table() (token ranges, resumable, throttled), drop old. LWT lock, waits for schema agreement. Argus didn't need it.
what-production-found: Facts to keep: exactly one coodie issue from the migration (coodie#271, VectorIndex name); everything else ran as released; you ran a full architecture review afterwards, fixes in 1.7.x. The quote below is my placeholder in Alexey's style: every detector flagged it. It must be replaced by Alexey's own words.
give-coodie-a-try: Facts to keep: Argus runs on coodie, fully async, same schema as under cqlengine. Thanks to Alexey. coodie is in the ScyllaDB GitHub org. cqlengine is in maintenance mode; from the next ScyllaDB Python driver release, importing it raises a DeprecationWarning pointing to coodie (python-driver#1127, yours). Call to action: try coodie, migration guide, Argus walkthrough, open issues. Pangram read only the last 61 words of the old version as human; they were mine too, so rewrite them anyway.
